title: Canva Launches Craft, Its First In-House Image Model Built for Design
excerpt: Trained on millions of human-made templates instead of photographs, Craft plans a layout before it renders — and is live now in Dream Lab and the Canva API.
body:
• Canva has launched Craft, its first in-house image generation model, built by Canva Research and trained on millions of human-designed templates rather than photographs.
  • Craft works in two stages — it plans layout, scale, hierarchy and text first, then renders at up to 2K resolution in 30 aspect ratios.
  • The model is live for all users in Dream Lab and through the Canva API, with access planned in ChatGPT and Gemini via Canva's MCP connector.
  • Cheaper Craft-fast and Craft-ultrafast variants are in development; owning the model cuts Canva's third-party API costs and gives it control over quality and speed.

Canva has released Craft, its first image generation model built entirely in-house, as the design platform moves to stop renting core AI technology from rivals. Developed by Canva Research, the company's in-house AI lab, Craft is aimed directly at image models from Google, OpenAI, ByteDance and Meta, according to TechCrunch and The Hindu's report of the launch. Canva announced the model in its official Craft announcement on October 22.

Plan first, then render

Most image models turn a prompt straight into pixels. Craft splits the work. In the first stage, it interprets the prompt and builds a plan covering the spatial relationships of elements, their relative scale, the visual hierarchy and the text that should appear. In the second stage, a rendering model turns that plan into an image at up to 2K resolution, in any of 30 aspect ratios for different platforms.

Canva says the approach produces accurate object details and legible text — the two failures that most often make AI images unusable for real design work. It also lets users make precise edits to one element without changing the rest of the image, and Craft can render text in images in 55 languages.

Trained on designs, not photographs

The training data is the other deliberate difference. Rather than training mainly on photographs, Canva trained Craft on human-designed templates from its own library — posters, social posts, presentations, infographics, menus and typography-rich layouts. That design-first diet is meant to make the output behave like a design, not a photo.

It also connects to Canva's existing tools. Images generated with Craft can be converted into layered, editable designs using Canva Magic Layers, the company's image-to-design transformer, building on the design-understanding model Canva released last year. Researchers from Leonardo.ai, the media generation platform Canva acquired in 2024, contributed to the new model.

Why Canva built its own model

Cost is a central reason. Canva has used a range of outside image models inside its platform, and those API bills add up at its scale. The company said owning Craft gives it better control over quality and speed as well as cost. That pressure has been visible this year: heavy use of third-party frontier models forced Canva to slow an earlier AI rollout and cut its expected annual revenue growth from 30% to 20%, after a year on track for about $4 billion in revenue.

Early benchmark claims are strong, though they are company-cited. Canva says Craft debuted fourth overall on DesignArena's independent image-generation leaderboard, ranked first for People & Portraits and for Landscapes & Nature, and second for Abstract & Patterns — results that would make Canva the second-highest-ranked image-generation lab behind OpenAI on that board.

Where to try it, and what comes next

Craft is available now to all Canva users from the Dream Lab tab, and to developers through the Canva API — the developer documentation pins it as model craft_v1_2k on the image-generations endpoint. Canva also plans to support generation inside third-party chatbots such as ChatGPT and Gemini through its MCP connector. Two lighter variants, Craft-fast and Craft-ultrafast, are in development to cut inference steps and cost.

For the large number of Indian and diaspora creators, marketers and small businesses who build social posts, menus and presentations in Canva every day, the practical test is simple: whether Craft's text stays readable and its layouts stay intact without an hour of cleanup. If it does, the model becomes a production tool rather than a novelty — and Canva keeps more of the value chain inside its own product.
